metadata.title: Exploring Validity Evidence for Mathematics Self-Concept of Adolescents: Key Findings from PISA 2022

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study used the publicly available PISA 2022 database and restricted the analysis to U.S. students who participated in PISA 2022 (n=4552). The authors report that sampling weights were used in all analyses to obtain precise parameter estimates and that multilevel modeling accounted for between-school clustering by employing replication weights. Analyses were conducted with the International Database (IDB) Analyzer v5.0.32 and SPSS v25, which are designed for complex survey handling in PISA. For missingness in mathematics achievement PVs, the authors applied a fully conditional specification approach with single imputation (10 iterations) prior to analysis; they do not report any additional outlier trimming or grade/school-type filtering beyond the U.S. restriction.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used only U.S. students who participated in PISA 2022; included 15- and 16-year-old adolescents. Mathematics performance was represented using PISA 2022 mathematics plausible values (10 sets) from the booklet design. Missing data in the study variables (11.9%–13.5% across variables) were imputed prior to analysis using fully conditional specification with single imputation and 10 iterations; no missing-by-design issue was applied to background questionnaire data.

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2022 Mathematics (U.S. students; mathematics self-concept index vs motivation index)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Chi-squared: χ2 = 86008.920 (df=1), p < .001; effect sizes: φ = 0.153, Cramer’s V = 0.153
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2022 Mathematics data (U.S. students), the study leveraged mathematics self-concept (relative index) to predict mathematics motivation (relative index), finding that mathematics self-concept was positively associated with mathematics motivation (χ2 = 86008.920, p < .001; φ = 0.153). This indicates that strengthening mathematics self-concept may align with higher mathematics motivation, supporting concurrent validity for the self-concept measure, though the cross-sectional association does not establish directionality.

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2022 Mathematics (U.S. students; mathematics self-concept index vs self-efficacy indices)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Point biserial correlation: rpb = -0.078, p < .001 (negative but negligible effect size)
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2022 Mathematics data (U.S. students), the study leveraged mathematics self-concept (relative index) to predict mathematics self-efficacy (formal/applied), finding a statistically significant but negligible negative association (rpb = -0.078, p < .001). This indicates that mathematics self-concept is meaningfully distinct from self-efficacy beliefs, supporting discriminant validity and suggesting that interventions should address these constructs separately.

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2022 Mathematics (U.S. students; mathematics self-concept index vs self-efficacy indices)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Point biserial correlation: rpb = -0.073, p < .001 (negative but negligible effect size)
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2022 Mathematics data (U.S. students), the study leveraged mathematics self-concept (relative index) to predict mathematics self-efficacy (reasoning/21st century), finding a statistically significant but negligible negative association (rpb = -0.073, p < .001). This indicates that mathematics self-concept captures a different psychological construct than self-efficacy, supporting discriminant validity and informing measurement and program design to avoid conflating the two.

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2022 Mathematics (U.S. students; mathematics self-concept index predicting mathematics performance PVs)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Multilevel model: standardized β = 0.08; unstandardized β = 20.20 (se = 4.28), t = 4.72, p < .001
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2022 Mathematics data (U.S. students), the study leveraged mathematics self-concept (relative index) to predict mathematics performance (plausible values), finding that mathematics self-concept significantly and positively predicted performance (β = 20.20, p < .001). This indicates that improving mathematics self-concept may be a promising lever for raising achievement, supporting predictive validity, while the observational design and multilevel modeling limit causal interpretation.

data.outcome_summary: The study examined validity evidence for a PISA 2022 mathematics self-concept construct using only U.S. students (n=4552). Mathematics self-concept was operationalized as a single relative index item (“Mathematics is easy for me” endorsed more than test language and science), and mathematics motivation was similarly coded as a relative index. Concurrent validity was supported by a significant positive association between self-concept and motivation (χ2 = 86008.920, p < .001; φ = 0.153). Discriminant validity was supported by statistically significant but negligible negative point-biserial correlations with two self-efficacy composites (rpb = -0.078 and -0.073, p < .001). Predictive validity was supported via multilevel modeling that accounted for school clustering using replication weights, showing self-concept predicted mathematics performance PVs (β = 20.20, p < .001). Limitations include single-item indices for motivation and self-concept and the non-causal, correlational nature of validity evidence.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This paper is not an empirical machine-learning prediction study: it evaluates psychometric validity evidence using chi-squared tests, point-biserial correlations, and multilevel modeling rather than training ML algorithms. As a result, ml_techniques.all_techniques is empty and no ML primary model can be identified. The study still uses PISA plausible values for mathematics performance and applies complex-survey weighting and replication weights in the multilevel analysis.
